svg.title: Brownian Motion vs OU Process
svg.desc: Brownian motion carries shocks forever; the OU process is pulled back to its long-run mean by a force proportional to the deviation.
svg.text: A continuous-time unit root vs continuous-time mean reversion
A constant μ, independent of the level
A pull proportional to the deviation
Drifts away from where it started
Shocks accumulate directly in the level
The restoring force is proportional to the deviation
The speed of return decides whether it is usable
Brownian motion carries shocks forever; OU is pulled toward θ in proportion to the deviation.
Model mean-reverting variables as OU and read the speed from the half-life.
Discretized at interval Δ it becomes an AR(1); the estimated φ gives κ and the half-life.
Next: the same OU applied to rates — Vasicek vs CIR.
